content:
Apple has started iOS 27.2 beta testing, and this update brings several notable changes and new features. Here's everything you need to know about iOS 27.2, which is expected to roll out to iPhone users as early as next month.

Why iOS 27.2 instead of iOS 27.1?

Apple released iOS 27 on September 14, bringing a host of new iPhone features including Siri AI. iOS 27.2 entered beta testing on September 16, two days later.

Where did iOS 27.1 go?

Apple previously confirmed that iPhone Duo will ship with iOS 27.1 pre-installed when it launches on October 23. This means iOS 27.1 contains a lot of iPhone Duo-related code, and Apple wants to keep it under wraps before the device goes on sale. So iOS 27.1 will be exclusive to iPhone Duo.

After that, the software paths for iPhone Duo and other iPhone models will converge, possibly through an iOS 27.2.x software update, or perhaps iOS 27.3.

So there will be a brief period where things don't run quite as smoothly, but ultimately everything will return to normal.

iOS 27.2 new features

Redesigned Health app

At the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, Apple showcased a brand-new version of the Health app and said it would arrive later this year. This new app has now entered beta testing with iOS 27.2.

The redesigned Health app is divided into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features a completely new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab adds a new Health age feature, which uses Apple Watch data to show how your various metrics compare to your actual age.

The new Health app is unlikely to launch alongside iOS 27.2 next month. Apple is simply beginning beta testing of this new app now, with a full rollout to all users coming later this year.

Learn more: iOS 27.2 completely overhauls the Apple Health app—here's a look at the new features

Profiles come to the TV app

The Apple TV app in iOS 27.2 adds profile support for the first time. This feature has been available on tvOS for several years, but this marks its debut on iPhone.

Learn more: iOS 27.2 brings new profile features to the Apple TV app on iPhone

More Siri AI language support

Siri AI is a key new feature of iOS 27, and iOS 27.2 expands it to more users. This update adds Siri AI support for the following languages:

  • French
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish

Dual-camera capture mode comes to Group FaceTime

In iOS 27, Apple introduced a brand-new Dual Capture feature for FaceTime, allowing you to activate both the front and rear cameras simultaneously. The other party can see not only you, but also what's in front of you. iOS 27.2 expands this feature to Group FaceTime calls for the first time.

Dual Capture requires an iPhone 17 or later, and all participants in the call must be running iOS 27.

Learn more: iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime's best new feature even better

Other minor changes

  • In Apple Podcasts, the "Up Next" playlist has been renamed to "New Episodes." The "Continue Playing" section now appears directly below New Episodes. The episode list also now uses backgrounds based on the podcast cover art colors.
  • Some red icons and accent elements in the Music app have been changed to black.
  • The Call Context feature in iOS 27 (which displays information directly on screen when calling merchants) has been expanded to include anniversaries.
  • There are minor changes to the alarm interface in the Clock app, such as smaller fonts for AM and PM labels.

A preview of more features to come

Finally, the iOS 27.2 code hints at several new features that may soon be coming to iPhone users, including real-time countdowns for new Apple Music album releases, third-party app support for "describe a shortcut," and new CarPlay Ultra themes. iOS 27.2 also shows that Apple continues to develop an iPhone anti-theft feature.

These features aren't enabled in iOS 27.2 yet, but the code indicates Apple is actively working on them internally.

iOS 27.2 release date

iOS 27.2 is expected to be pushed out to iPhone users sometime in October. Apple has promised that Siri AI will gain more languages in October, and iOS 27.2 adds exactly these new languages, so the update must launch before November for Apple to keep that promise.

Wrap-up

Are you running the iOS 27.2 beta? Have you discovered any useful new features? What do you think of the new Health app? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
